text:
Alex: FYI saw a weird perf spike on m7b + sliding-window when we enabled TTL-based KV eviction on canary. tail lat jumped ~3x for a subset of requests.

Priya: Interesting — did kernel chooser flip at the same time?

Alex: Yup. The runtime switched from the small-matrix kernel to the generic fallback for ~40% of the tokens after eviction happened. Logs show kernel_selector choosing `matmul_generic` instead of `matmul_tiled` right after a `kv_evict` event.

Ken: Can you paste the exact log lines?

Alex: Here are the relevant snippets:

```
[2248503333.112] KVCache: evict prefix len 512 -> new_kv_len=64
[2248503333.113] KernelChooser: reported seq_len=576, chosen_kernel=matmul_generic (est_cost=2.8)
[2248503333.114] Runtime: selected kernel matmul_generic, batch=1, heads=16, head_dim=64
[2248503333.115] Perf: tail_p50=22ms tail_p99=310ms
```

Sam: Looks like eviction reduces the cached prefix but the kernel estimator still reads an outdated sequence-length distribution and overestimates cost of the tiled kernel. We should be invalidating the estimator's warm path on KV mutation.

Priya: Agreed. Also saw a reproducer: run a 1k token prompt with periodic short completions to trigger TTL evict and measure. Script we used: 

```
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -X POST $CANARY_API -d '{"input": "<1k prompt>"}'; sleep 0.3; done
```

Ken: Perf numbers from the canary run (avg over 50 queries):

```
before-ttl: tail_p99=95ms, avg_token=6.2ms
after-ttl:  tail_p99=312ms, avg_token=18.9ms
```

Priya: Oof. That lines up with kernel flip. Two possible fixes: 1) force estimator recalculation on KV eviction (cheap), 2) make kernel chooser use conservative fallback that prefers tiled kernel if KV length just changed but batch is small.

Alex: Option 1 seems simplest to try. Where is the estimator state stored? I can PR to invalidate the cached profile on `kv_eviction()` event.

Sam: It's in runtime/metrics/kernel_cost_cache. You need to clear the per-model seqdist entry. Also consider adding a short TTL on that cache entry (5s) so transient evicts don't persist in estimator.

Ken: Quick thought on root cause — our `seq_len_est` derives from last N requests, but evictions create a discontinuity: code assumes cached prefix persists which affects the effective seq_len. Maybe update the estimator to track `kv_age` and bias older samples down.

Priya: Good idea. For immediate mitigation, put a rollout: disable TTL eviction for <2k context sessions in Dedicated canary and patch estimator. Can we patch + redeploy canary tonight?

deploy-bot: scheduled canary redeploy to `runtime-canary-2` at 2024-11-07T02:10:00Z — rolling with image `gcr/redwood/runtime:canary-2248`

Alex: I'll open a small PR with two commits: (A) invalidate kernel_cost_cache on kv_evict, (B) add 5s soft-ttl to estimator entries. Will link PR here once ready.

perf-bot: quick profile summary attached: delta shows 3.2x increase in GEMM time for affected tokens when using `matmul_generic` vs `matmul_tiled` on A100. See perf-bot report: https://perf.redwood.internal/reports/2248503333

Sam: Thanks. Action items:
- Alex: PR for cache invalidation + soft-ttl (ETA 4h)
- Ken: add seq_age feature to estimator design doc (ETA EOD)
- Priya: patch rollout plan to disable TTL for small sessions (ETA 1h)

Ken: I'll also add a unit test that simulates a KV eviction and asserts kernel chooser prefers tiled kernel for small batches.

Alex: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/5042 — small changes, unit + integration test included. Can reviewers please take a look?

Priya: Reviewing now. If green, promote to canary after deploy window. :thumbsup:

Sam: Nice catch — this explains the regression pattern we were seeing in customer traces where queries do short back-and-forths and then see latency spikes.

Alex: Will monitor canary once deployed and post a short follow-up.

Priya: Thanks everyone.
